name: Avivo Bio Inc.
description: Avivo Bio is developing an enzymatic platform technology to convert blood types A, B, and AB into universal type O blood for both transfusion and organ transplantation. The company's Enzyme Converted Type O (ECO) technology addresses blood type incompatibility, a 125-year constraint in medicine, by removing blood group antigens to expand usable donor supply and save lives.
nextMilestone: IDE submission and first-in-human feasibility studies for deceased donor ECO transplant and blood ECO transfusion

name: Cellis AG
description: Cellis has developed a novel macrophage-based immunotherapy platform for solid tumors using the TRAIN mechanism. The platform delivers intracellular payloads via ferritin-drug complexes to trigger pattern recognition-based immune activation, overcoming antigen escape and tumor heterogeneity while generating durable anti-tumor immunity.
nextMilestone: Phase I clinical trial initiation in glioblastoma and head & neck cancer

name: Link Biologics
description: Link Biologics is developing first-in-class protein biologics for inflammatory and degenerative disorders. The company's lead program, LB001, is a multifunctional therapeutic for dry eye disease that both repairs tissue and reduces inflammation, addressing both drivers of the disease cycle. LB001 has demonstrated superior preclinical efficacy to Restasis with 50% of eyes showing no signs of DED after 7 days at the highest doses.

name: Azalla Pharmaceuticals
description: Azalla Pharmaceuticals is developing two oral small molecule compounds from a single proprietary chemical class for rare neuro-immune diseases. J-041 is the lead asset targeting dermatomyositis (an orphan indication with one approved IV therapy), while J-019 is a dual-mechanism compound for multiple sclerosis that combines CB2 agonism with PPARγ activation.
nextMilestone: Orphan drug designation filing (December 2026) followed by IND filing for J-041 (Q4 2027)

name: Repairon Immuno GmbH
description: Repairon Immuno develops cellular medicines to rejuvenate the adaptive immune system using iPSC-derived cell therapies. The company's platform includes booster cells to enhance immune function, suppressor cells to modulate chronic inflammation, and technology to rebuild immune organs such as artificial thymus and lymph nodes, addressing autoimmune disorders, hematopoietic cancers, and age-related immune dysfunction.

name: Lophora ApS
description: Lophora is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing long-acting, selective 5-HT2AR therapeutics for rapid, durable treatment of depression and neuropsychiatric disorders. Their lead asset LPH-5 is designed for once-daily, at-home administration with sustained sub-perceptual exposure, eliminating the need for clinic-intensive delivery while targeting Major Depressive Disorder initially with expansion potential across anxiety and stress-related disorders.

name: TQ Therapeutics (TQx)
description: TQ Therapeutics is a Germany-based cell therapy company developing a modular hybrid in vivo platform (CELLfinity) for scalable next-generation cell and gene therapy workflows. The platform combines ex vivo control and safety with the simplicity and scalability of in vivo approaches through an ultra-fast, bedside-compatible workflow that enables rapid target-cell selection, controlled genetic modification, and reinfusion. The company is advancing a lead autoimmune CAR-T program (TQ-1001) while positioning the platform for multiple therapeutic indications and pharma partnerships.
nextMilestone: IND filing and initiation of Phase I/IIa clinical trial for TQ-1001 autoimmune CAR-T program

name: Morphian Therapeutics
description: Morphian Therapeutics is a UK-based biotech company developing DD-2401, a LAMP2B mRNA therapy delivered via a novel cardiotropic lipid nanoparticle (LNP) platform for Danon disease. The company has demonstrated cardiac protein expression, endpoint normalization, and favorable safety in preclinical studies, and is advancing toward non-human primate toxicology studies and first-in-human clinical trials.

name: Link Biologics
description: Link Biologics is pioneering first-in-class protein biologics for inflammatory and degenerative disorders. The company's lead program, LB001, targets Dry Eye Disease (DED) with a multifunctional mechanism that both repairs tissue and reduces inflammation, demonstrating superior preclinical efficacy to existing treatments like Restasis.

name: CRYOVASC GmbH
description: CRYOVASC is developing the Renal Freezer, the world's first cryoballoon catheter for renal denervation to treat drug-resistant hypertension. The device uses cryoablation (freezing) technology to ablate overactive kidney nerves that drive high blood pressure, demonstrating up to 6× more effective denervation compared to existing heat-based devices in preclinical studies published in JACC.

name: chimeris
description: Owner: Shamim Dadvar | Segment: Therapeutics | Field: Autoimmune disease | Dev stage (src): Pre-clinic | Current project: Chimeris is a cell therapy company company with a novel in vivo drug delivery platform focused on treatments for autoimmune diseases, solid tumours and liquid tumours. The company is developing SENDER-ULTRA, a novel technology platform for multi-modular in vivo CAR-T which allows for significant costs reduction while improving the scalability of CGT. SENDER-ULTRA is based on 2 proprietary technologies: SENDER (in vivo CAR delivery system via mRNA-LNP) and COMPACT (CAR-T with multiple engineered genes designed for solid tumours). With dual targeting, NS503 their lead multi-modular in vivo CAR-T delivers strong in vivo efficacy with only a fraction of the LNP dosage required. In addition, the transfection with SENDER is safe and controllable with significantly reduced off-target effects in hepatocytes. Chimeris have shown that SENDER technology can be efficiently used to retarget all major ionizable lipid formulations, allowing for scalable and low-cost manufacturing. Since demonstrating preclinical POC for its in vivo SENDER platform in a mouse model in 2024, Chimeris have made meaningful progress on both their mRNA and LNP-SENDER platforms, as well as on the CMC front. Their mRNA expression shows high specificity to T cells, which not only enhances overall targeting precision but also enables the inclusion of additional armouring elements. Meanwhile, their LNP-SENDER demonstrates improved cell specificity and a simplified structure, which in turn streamlines the CMC process and reduces cost. Chimeris now have a clear path forward on CMC, supported by a large CDMO partnership. Both process development and analytical development are well underway. Notably, although currently 6–9 months behind Capstan largely due to resource constraints, considering all available data, Chimeris’s lead candidate appears to be more potent than Capstan’s—achieving similar or better effect with just 10% of the dose. NHP studies will start this summer, with Investigator-Initiated Trials (IIT) planned by year-end. With timely funding, Chimeris aim to gather systematic human data ahead of competitors. | Submitted: 07/24/2025 | Last update: 07/24/2025 | Legacy ID: 742944

name: Cytoki
description: Cytoki Pharma is a pioneering biotechnology company focused on developing innovative treatments for serious diseases using IL-22 based drugs. IL-22 is a protein that plays a crucial role in immune response, tissue protection, and metabolism. The company is leveraging this biology to create a new class of medicines aimed at treating metabolic diseases, which include conditions like obesity and diabetes. Cytoki Pharma's lead product, CK 0045, is a long-acting IL-22 analog currently in Phase 1 clinical trials. These trials are designed to evaluate the safety and tolerability of the drug in healthy participants, both with and without obesity. The results from these trials are expected in the first half of 2024. This drug has shown promising preclinical data, demonstrating its potential to reduce weight and improve glucose control, which are critical factors in managing metabolic diseases. The company operates in the biotechnology and pharmaceutical market, primarily targeting healthcare providers and patients dealing with metabolic and epithelial-related diseases. Their business model revolves around research and development (R&D) of new drugs, followed by clinical trials, regulatory approval, and eventually, commercialization. Cytoki Pharma generates revenue through funding rounds, such as their successful $45 million Series A raise, and will eventually make money by selling their approved drugs to healthcare providers and patients. In summary, Cytoki Pharma is at the forefront of developing IL-22 based treatments that could revolutionize the management of metabolic diseases. Their innovative approach and promising early data position them as a key player in the biotechnology sector. description: Dopavision is a therapeutic company developing a digital therapeutic for myopia. Myopia, or shortsightedness, is a condition where the visual image is focused in front of the retina, instead of on the retina itself, as it should. People with myopia have good near sight vision but poor distance vision. Dopavision is developing a digital therapeutic for myopia which can be seamlessly and invisibly integrated with the use of a smartphone. Myopia is a visual condition that affects on average every third person globally, a share that has increased rapidly during the last two decades. The goal of the Berlin-based startup is to develop a clinically validated therapy for myopia progression in children and adolescents. name: Draupnir
description: Draupnir Bio is a Danish biotechnology company established in 2017 as a spin-out from Aarhus University and the Max-Planck Society. The company was co-founded by Professors Simon Glerup, Camilla Gustafsen, Peder Madsen, and Peter Seeberger, based on their research into the biology of proteins implicated in disease. Simon Glerup, who has a PhD in molecular biology and postdoctoral experience in neuroscience, was the founding CEO and led the company's initial financing rounds before transitioning to the role of Chief Scientific Officer. The company's core focus is pioneering the next stage of targeted protein degradation (TPD), a field that uses a cell's own disposal mechanisms to eliminate disease-causing proteins. While first-generation TPD therapies are limited to targets inside the cell (cytosolic targets), Draupnir's proprietary platform develops oral, small-molecule degraders that can target extracellular and membrane-bound proteins. This approach significantly expands the range of treatable targets, as these proteins make up about 40% of the human proteome and have been historically difficult to address with conventional drugs. The technology utilizes lysosome receptors to remove these pathogenic proteins, with initial applications aimed at cardiovascular disease, as well as inflammatory and neurological disorders. Draupnir Bio operates on a standard biotechnology business model, focusing on research and development to build a preclinical pipeline. Its financial strategy relies on venture capital investment to fund its R&D activities toward developing commercially viable therapeutics. The company has successfully raised significant capital through multiple funding rounds. In 2019, it secured €30 million in a Series A round from investors including Novo Seeds, Gilde Healthcare, Inkef Capital, and High-Tech Gründerfonds. More recently, in July 2024, the company raised an additional €12 million in a seed round. This round brought in new investors MP Healthcare (the venture arm of Mitsubishi Tanabe Pharma Corporation) and the Export and Investment Fund of Denmark (EIFO), alongside continued support from its existing backers. These funds are allocated to advancing its preclinical pipeline of oral protein degraders. name: ErVimmune
description: ErVimmune, a biotechnology company, spin-off of Centre Léon Bérard (CLB) and Centre de Recherche en Cancérologie de Lyon (CRCL) (Lyon, France), incorporated in October 2019, is developing next-generation cancer vaccines and T-cell therapies. Its mission is to address a persistent therapeutic challenge for patients who do not respond to current immunotherapies and to open new therapeutic opportunities in the treatment of cancers with high unmet medical needs, such as Triple Negative Breast Cancer (TNBC) and ovarian cancer. Vaccine and T-cell based therapies represent therapeutics of choice to convert immunologically “cold tumors” into “hot tumors”. There is a need to identify new tumor antigens, shared across patients in a same disease, as therapeutic targets for off-the-shelf cancer vaccine and T-cell based therapies, especially for tumors with a low/moderate tumor mutational burden (TMB). Human endogenous retroviruses (HERVs) answered these two criteria. They represent a significant part of the human genome (8%) and are kept silent by epigenetic regulation in healthy cells. HERVs are aberrantly expressed during malignant transformation and represent a reservoir of targetable antigens, especially in tumors with a low or moderate TMB. As HERV-derived antigens are shared across patients, they represent a particularly well-suited approach for developing off-the-shelf immunotherapies for solid tumors. We demonstrated that HERV-derived antigens represent a source of shared tumor epitopes, which that can induce strong anti-tumor T- cell responses thanks to our proprietary bioinformatics platform to identify potential epitope candidates that are then supported by proteomics and immunology assays data. name: Gesynta Pharma
description: Founded in 2017, Gesynta Pharma bases its R&D on research from the Karolinska Institutet. Gesynta Pharma aims to exploit the full potential of microsomal prostaglandin E synthase-1 (mPGES-1) as a pharmacological target by developing inhibitors in areas of unmet medical need where mPGES-1 inhibition provides a clear differentiation. Major shareholders include Industrifonden, Linc, Hadean Ventures, and a number of successful life science entrepreneurs. In a recently completed clinical phase II study, the most advanced drug candidate, GS-248, was evaluated with regards to its safety profile, its ability to inhibit mPGES-1, as well as its effect on Raynaud’s phenomenon and peripheral blood flow in systemic sclerosis patients. After treatment, no significant effects were seen compared to placebo in terms of symptomatic relief in patients with systemic sclerosis. For the first time in patients, however, the Phase II study confirmed the tolerability and safety profile, pharmacokinetics, and unique ability of GS-248 to inhibit mPGES-1 and thus modify prostaglandin profile. name: Micreos
description: According to the World Health Organization (WHO) emergence of antibiotic-resistant 'superbugs' is now a global concern, which can spell the end of modern medicine and a return to the days when routine operations, simple wounds or straightforward infections were potentially life-threatening. On the other hand scientists have come to realize that the vast majority of bacteria is beneficial and should be left intact. Antibiotics do not distinguish between bad and good bacteria and their use can lead to side effects and resistance. Micreos develops the world's first targeted antibacterial products, set to replace antibiotics. With Micreos' endolysin technology, for the first time it is possible to kill only the unwanted bacteria - including antibiotic resistant strains such as MRSA - while leaving our microbiome - comprising billions of beneficial bacteria on our skin and in our gut - intact. In addition, research shows that the use of endolysins does not induce resistance. This unlocks a completely new approach in dealing with the bacteria around us: killing the bad bacteria and preserving the microbiome. Micreos' Staphefekt SA.100 is an enzyme (endolysin), that targets only Staphylococcus aureus. Marketed under the Gladskin brand, it is the world's first endolysin registered for human use and has had a life-changing impact for thousands of people suffering from inflammatory skin conditions such as eczema, inflammatory acne and rosacea and resistant wound infections (see www.gladskin.com). A series of pharmaceutical products based on the endolysin XZ.700 - also targeting S. aureus - is in clinical development. First indications include: atopic dermatitis, diabetic wound infections and folliculitis. Micreos has also developed FDA-approved food safety products: 'Phageguard S' against Salmonella and 'Phageguard L' against Listeria monocytogenes, which is especially dangerous for pregnant women and for the elderly and immuno-compromised (www.phageguard.com).  ||  Owner: tyra.kuller | Total raised to date: 105,700,000 | Employees: 11-50 | Founded: 01/01/2006 | Investors: Horizon 2020, Ministry of Economic Affairs (Innovation Credit) | Keywords: Biotechnology, Health Care, Product Design, Product Research | Submitted: 12/05/2025 | Last update: 04/22/2026 | Legacy ID: 773373

name: immunobrain
description: Owner: Shamim Dadvar | Segment: Therapeutics | Field: Neurodegenerative diseases | Dev stage (src): Phase I | Current project: to ImmunoBrain, a private clinical stage biotech company developing a proprietary checkpoint inhibitor to treat neurodegenerative disease. The underlying mechanistic approach, pioneered by Prof Michal Schwarz at the Weizmann Institute, is focused on alleviating immune system exhaustion in the brain, and enabling restored immune function to dampen neuroinflammation, a common pathological feature shared across many neurodegenerative diseases. The therapeutic mechanism of action the company is employing is highly unique - activation of a common peripheral immune system pathway with a specially optimized checkpoint inhibitor, which triggers a cascade that sends immune regulatory cells such as monocytes and TRegs to the brain to restore immune function (i.e., the treatment itself is targeted at the immune system, not the brain). This is a first-in-class approach with potential disease modifying potential across a range of neurodegenerative diseases. The company is conducting an ongoing Phase 1b SAD/MAD trial of their IBC-Ab002 checkpoint inhibitor in Alzheimer’s, designed to demonstrate safety and provide proof of mechanism. Enrollment was completed in late 2024, and the company recently conducted a pre-specified interim analysis from the trial that showed encouraging safety to date, dose dependent activation of the peripheral immune system, and correlated reductions in GFAP, a biomarker of neuroinflammation. I am looking to connect with potential investors to introduce the story in advance of the full data set which will be available in early 2026. Results will dictate a go-forward funding strategy that could include a substantial private fundraising effort. | Submitted: 07/31/2025 | Last update: 07/31/2025 | Legacy ID: 743839

name: Lucy Therapeutics
description: Lucy Therapeutics is a biotech company providing effective treatments for neurological diseases start with the mitochondria. They offering a differentiated and novel approach to drug discovery by drugging targets associated with early disease pathogenesis. Their innovative approach can also be expanded to provide new options for treating similar neurologically focused diseases including Parkinson's Disease (PD) and Alzheimer's Disease (AD). name: Qu Biologics
description: Qu Biologics Inc. is a private, clinical-stage biotechnology company based in Vancouver, Canada, focused on developing treatments for diseases linked to chronic inflammation. Founded in 2007 by Dr. Hal Gunn and Rob Freeman, the company is pioneering a novel immunotherapy platform called Site Specific Immunomodulators (SSIs). Dr. Gunn, who serves as CEO, is a physician-entrepreneur with a long-standing interest in the body's innate healing capacities. His journey began after witnessing a remarkable recovery in a pancreatic cancer patient who developed a severe infection, leading him to hypothesize that activating the innate immune system could combat chronic diseases. Before founding Qu Biologics, Dr. Gunn co-founded InspireHealth, Canada's foremost supportive cancer care center, and he holds a Doctorate of Medicine from the University of British Columbia. The company's core business revolves around its proprietary SSI platform, which is designed to restore normal immune function in specific organs. Unlike immunotherapies that target a single pathway, SSIs are developed to stimulate and 'train' the body's innate immune system, directing activated immune cells to a targeted organ to resolve the underlying immune dysfunction. The technology is based on the 'hygiene hypothesis,' which links a decline in acute infections to a rise in immune-related diseases. SSIs are composed of components from inactivated bacteria that are typically associated with infections in the target organ, aiming to mimic the beneficial training effects of an infection without causing illness. For example, QBECO, which targets the gastrointestinal tract, is derived from E. coli, while QBKPN targets the lungs and is derived from K. pneumoniae. The treatments are designed for self-administration via subcutaneous injection. Qu Biologics is a clinical-stage company, generating data through a series of clinical trials rather than commercial revenue. The company serves patients with conditions such as cancer (lung, colon), inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis), and immunosenescence (age-related immune decline). Qu Biologics has completed several Phase 2 clinical trials and has others underway to evaluate the safety and efficacy of its SSI treatments. As a private entity, the firm's operations are financed through equity funding from angel investors, family offices, and high-net-worth individuals, along with non-dilutive funding from grants. The company has raised approximately $29.8M in total funding, including a $12M Series C round in March 2022, to advance its clinical programs and expand its team. name: Rouge Therapeutics
description: Segment: Therapeutics | Field: Haematology | Dev stage (src): Phase I | Current project: We are: • Developing a small molecule therapeutic at Development Candidate stage (RTX-001) • Raising €/$ 35m+ to Ph2a and exit • Focusing on a large rare disease, HHT - no approved treatments ($bns market) • Reducing risk of drug development by re-engineering commercial molecules with off-label clinical data • Supported by an Expert / Experienced team Rouge Therapeutics is advancing first-in-class proprietary small molecule enhancers of blood vessel stabilization and pericyte attachment with an initial focus on hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT). The company’s drug discovery is clinically derisked though re-engineering clinical and commercial compounds that have shown efficacy in randomized placebo controlled randomized HHT clinical trials. Rouge’s lead small molecule is close to DC nomination with proven efficacy in multiple HHT models, demonstrated preclinical safety, excellent developability profile, and composition of matter IP. Our lead molecule/NCE (RTX-001) is differentiated from other molecules in development (which only regulate angiogenesis) as it enhances pericyte attachment to the endothelial cells. Pericyte attachment is critical for vascular stability, maturation, and prevention of AVMs (arterial venous malformation). This process plays a fundamental role in HHT, as well as diseases like diabetic retinopathy, neurovascular and neurodegenerative diseases. We have also shown that enhanced pericyte attachment is regulated by PDGF-β secretion in endothelial cells, and that thalidomide, pomalidomide (IMiDs) and our lead molecule increase the expression of PDGF-β secretion (both in vitro and in in vivo models). We have determined that the upregulation of PDGF-β secretion is not mediated by cereblon as we removed the cereblon pharmacophore in RTX-001. The safety profile of RTX-001 is far superior to IMiDs as demonstrated in 7-day toxicology, 12-day rat teratogenicity, and have initiated a 7day dog DRF with the goal of declaring a Development Candidate in August. The company is presently raising a $35M+ Series A to end of Phase 2a clinical studies in HHT. | Submitted: 08/14/2025 | Last update: 06/15/2026 | Legacy ID: 750162

name: Targovax
description: Targovax AS develops active immunotherapy in the form of cancer vaccines. The lead candidate TG01 is currently in a phase I/II clinical trial in resectable pancreatic cancer. Patients are treated after operation, and the immune system is triggered to recognize cancer specific RAS mutations and kill the cancer cells. TG01 consists of peptides designed to trigger both a helper- and cytotoxic T-cell response in the patients, ensuring a broad and lasting immune response. The Targovax peptides are designed for induction of RAS mutation specific T-helper cells through presentation on HLA class II molecules on the surface of Antigen Presenting Cells (APCs), but also for natural processing to potential HLA class I epitopes and induction of RAS mutation specific cytotoxic T cells.The T helper (Th) cells have a central and critical role in coordination of immune reactions and are often referred to as the ''generals'' and ''conductors'' of the immune system. The drug candidate has a strong historical background including clinical data. The clinical data indicate both an increase of mean survival and long-term survivors. The drug is well tolerated with a low degree of side effects. The company operates in the biopharmaceutical market, serving a broad range of clients including hospitals, healthcare providers, and patients suffering from AIS. TargED's business model revolves around the research, development, and commercialization of its clot-busting therapy. The company generates revenue through the sale of its products to healthcare providers and institutions. TargED is led by a team of seasoned professionals with extensive experience in drug development and commercialization. The company is currently in the process of strengthening its team, with recent job postings for a Head of Clinical Operations and a Medical Director. The company also recently appointed Erik van den Berg as Chair of its Supervisory Board and established a Scientific Advisory Board dedicated to the development of Microlyse. In summary, TargED Biopharmaceuticals is a promising startup in the biopharmaceutical sector, with a focus on developing targeted therapies for AIS. The company's innovative approach, combined with its experienced leadership team, positions it well for future growth in the healthcare market. name: Verigraft
description: VERIGRAFT is an innovative biotechnology startup based in Gothenburg, Sweden, specializing in personalized tissue-engineered transplants. The company has successfully completed preclinical development for its personalized tissue-engineered veins (P-TEV) and is now ready to commence clinical trials. VERIGRAFT's groundbreaking approach involves creating fully biological transplants that do not require immunosuppression, which is the process of reducing the effectiveness of the immune system to prevent it from attacking the transplanted tissue. VERIGRAFT's primary clients include healthcare providers, hospitals, and medical research institutions that are looking for advanced solutions to improve patient outcomes in vascular surgeries. The company operates in the regenerative medicine market, which focuses on repairing or replacing damaged tissues and organs through innovative medical treatments. The business model of VERIGRAFT revolves around developing and commercializing its patented RC (Reconditioning) process. This process uses a small sample of the patient's own blood, which is enriched with growth factors, nutrients, and balancing agents. This enriched culture medium is then used to recondition and repopulate a cell-free scaffold, resulting in a blood vessel that closely resembles the patient's own tissue. This significantly reduces the risk of thrombosis (blood clots) and infection compared to synthetic grafts. VERIGRAFT generates revenue by partnering with healthcare institutions and selling its personalized tissue-engineered transplants. The company also seeks funding through innovation grants and investments to support its research and development efforts. In summary, VERIGRAFT is at the forefront of regenerative medicine, offering personalized, fully biological transplants that promise greater durability and resistance to infection without the need for immunosuppression. Keywords: biotechnology, personalized transplants, regenerative medicine, tissue engineering, vascular surgery, clinical trials, immunosuppression-free, healthcare innovation, durable grafts, infection resistance.  ||  Owner: carl.kilander@healthcap.eu | Total raised to date: 5,400,000 | Last funding amount: 2,400,000 | Employees: 13 | Founded: 01/01/2005 | Keywords: Manufacturing, Health | Submitted: 09/11/2024 | Last update: 10/14/2024 | Legacy ID: 654086

name: Kivu Bioscience

Their platform uses site-specific GlycoConnect conjugation technology with lower DAR (drug-to-antibody ratio) and stable linkers to achieve wider therapeutic indices, enabling higher dosing and longer duration of therapy compared to existing ADCs.

items.question: Is the MoA relevant for the disease of interest?
Can results from preclinical models reliably be translated to clinical disease?
Will the molecule reach the target in sufficient quantity?
Is the molecule safe and are there specific tolerability questions?
Is manufacturing feasible at relevant clinical scale?
Is it possible to prove the TPP in a realistic time, recruit patients, and establish a dosing regimen? Is there a clear regulatory path (endpoints etc)?
Is there IP to allow adequate protection from competition?
What aspect in the technology/target will be the main differentiator to competitors?
